# 14. Multilingual / Internationalisation

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Make multilingual and multi-regional static sites understandable, accessible, crawlable, and culturally credible.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A locale strategy defining languages, regions, URL structure, default locale, fallback behavior, and translation ownership.
- [ ] A localized sitemap or sitemap entries for every indexable language version.
- [ ] Hreflang annotations for equivalent localized pages, including x-default where appropriate.
- [ ] Correct html lang attributes for every page and dir attributes for right-to-left languages where needed.
- [ ] Localized metadata, titles, descriptions, Open Graph tags, schema, form labels, validation messages, and legal links.
- [ ] A translation quality standard covering human review, terminology, tone, units, currency, date formats, addresses, phone formats, and cultural references.
- [ ] A language switcher standard with native language names, current language state, and equivalent-page linking.
- [ ] A missing-translation policy for pages not available in every locale.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Each localized URL must serve one clear language or regional variant.
- [ ] Hreflang URLs must be canonical, reciprocal, and point to equivalent content when possible.
- [ ] The language switcher must not send users to the homepage when an equivalent page exists.
- [ ] Machine translation must not be published as final premium content without human review.
- [ ] Localized pages must adapt proof, offers, units, addresses, legal expectations, and examples.
- [ ] Forms must accept local name, phone, address, and text input patterns.
- [ ] Text expansion must not break UI components or buttons.
- [ ] Localized schema must use content visible in the same locale.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check every page for correct lang, canonical, hreflang set, title, description, and localized internal links.
- [ ] Check reciprocal hreflang links across all equivalent pages.
- [ ] Check that locale paths are consistent, such as /en/, /es/, or region-specific variants.
- [ ] Check that date, time, currency, measurement, punctuation, and phone formats match locale expectations.
- [ ] Check that translated CTAs fit buttons and preserve intent.
- [ ] Check that legal, privacy, cookie, and consent text is appropriate for each target jurisdiction.
- [ ] Check that right-to-left layouts mirror only where appropriate and preserve brand and usability.
- [ ] Check that search engines are not blocked from localized pages.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid auto-redirecting users by IP without a visible override.
- [ ] Avoid mixing languages on one page except intentional names, quotes, or legal text.
- [ ] Avoid using flags as the only language selector.
- [ ] Avoid canonicalizing all language versions to one language.
- [ ] Avoid publishing translated pages without localized metadata.
- [ ] Avoid assuming hreflang replaces good content or correct language detection.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Each locale must feel intentionally written for that audience.
- [ ] Localized navigation, forms, metadata, and proof must be complete, not partial.
- [ ] Search engines must understand language alternatives from static markup.
- [ ] The site must remain maintainable as languages are added or removed.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to flag missing lang attributes, missing hreflang, inconsistent canonical URLs, and untranslated metadata patterns.
- [ ] Use static reports to compare locale coverage across URL sets.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Each language has a clear URL structure, complete translated pages, visible language switcher, equivalent-page links, translated navigation/footer/forms/errors/legal/metadata/alt text, and no accidental mixed language.
- [ ] Hreflang points to correct reciprocal live URLs, uses correct codes, matches canonicals, excludes broken/redirected targets where possible, and is updated when pages are added.
- [ ] Language-specific analytics, forms, CTAs, sitemap entries, legal pages, assets, fonts, cultural wording, dates, phone/address formats, and accessibility statement are checked.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
